brief: UBS sales desk commentary (06-Nov-2026) across three themes. US: October NFP forecast at +70k, mostly private payrolls (+65k), with an unemployment rate of 4.2%. Wage growth is forecast at +2.9%, which would be the lowest reading this cycle. Fed's Williams signaled the FOMC remains on a gradual tightening bias but sees no sign of troublesome inflation. UBS frames the labor market run-rate as robust, with private payrolls diffusion at cycle highs. Japan: nominal cash earnings beat at 4.6% (vs 3.8% est.) and real cash earnings beat at 2.2% (vs 1.3% est.), the strongest run-rate on record, reinforcing the BoJ's hiking cycle (JPY 1y1y at 1.87% implies slightly more than two hikes). Despite that hawkish data, JGBs rallied today in a flight-to-quality move comparable to USTs the prior day, bidding the curve outside 30y by 10bps+. G10 FX saw a nearly 2-std-dev safe-haven move, and EM FX moved sharply (USDTWD -2.3 std dev, USDINR -1.6 std dev). Canada: PM Carney's budget centers on an investment supercycle funneling energy revenue into capex, with limited near-term CAD impact given Canada's fiscal latitude from its net debt position.
